sourceCopy.name: Circle Calculator
sourceCopy.title: Circle Calculator Free | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Find circle area, circumference, diameter, arcs, sectors and segments. Free online calculator with clear formulas and examples.
sourceCopy.intro: Calculate a circle from its radius, diameter, area or circumference. Explore central-angle arc and sector measurements, or calculate a circular segment with its chord and sagitta.
sourceCopy.howQuestion: How do you calculate a circle?
sourceCopy.howAnswer: For radius r, diameter is 2r, circumference is 2πr and area is πr². For a central angle θ in radians, arc length is rθ and sector area is r²θ/2. This calculator converts an entered angle in degrees to radians for those formulas.
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. The formulas run in this browser and this tool does not upload or save your measurements.

fields.angleHint: Use an angle from 0 to 360 degrees. The formulas convert it to radians.
fields.accuracyNote: Uses exact circle formulas with the JavaScript value of π; displayed decimals are rounded. A circular segment uses the selected central angle: below 180° it is the minor segment, above 180° it is the major segment. Inputs are limited to positive values up to 10¹² and angles from 0° to 360°.

messages.checkInputs: Check the selected mode, measurements and angle.
messages.copyUnavailable: Copy is not available in this browser.

additionalFaqs.question: What are the area and circumference of a circle with radius 1?
additionalFaqs.answer: The area is π (about 3.14159) and the circumference is 2π (about 6.28318). Results are rounded for display.

additionalFaqs.question: How do I calculate arc length?
additionalFaqs.answer: Multiply the radius by the central angle in radians. This tool accepts degrees and converts them before calculating.

additionalFaqs.question: What is the difference between a sector and a segment?
additionalFaqs.answer: A sector is bounded by two radii and an arc. A segment is bounded by a chord and its arc; its area is calculated here from the central angle.
